title_en: Ningxia Yinghai Building Materials Group Co., Ltd. v. Ningxia Yinghai Yinchuan Building Materials Co., Ltd. and third party China Petroleum Ningxia Chemical Plant — dispute over creditor's rights
ruling_gist_en: In cases where a shareholder claims that a creditor-debtor relationship exists between the shareholder and the company, and the company acknowledges such relationship, but other shareholders of the company raise objections thereto, the people's court shall conduct a comprehensive analysis of the evidence from all parties. If the evidence is insufficient to prove the existence of such creditor-debtor relationship, the people's court shall not recognize that creditor-debtor relationship.

full_text_en:
Ningxia Yinghai Building Materials Group Co., Ltd. v.
Ningxia Yinghai Yinchuan Building Materials Co., Ltd. and Third Party:
China Petroleum Ningxia Chemical Plant — dispute over creditor's rights

【Ruling Summary】

In a case where a shareholder claims the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship with the company and the company acknowledges it, but other shareholders of the company raise objections, the people's court shall conduct a comprehensive analysis of the evidence submitted by all parties. If the evidence is insufficient to prove the existence of the creditor-debtor relationship, the people's court shall not recognize the creditor-debtor relationship.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2010) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 19

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Ningxia Yinghai Building Materials Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: South of Gucheng Township, Zhongning County, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.
Legal Representative: Lou Yan, General Manager of the company.
Agent ad litem: Tang Laifa, Legal Counsel of the company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Ningxia Yinghai Yinchuan Building Materials Co., Ltd. Domicile: Five Kilometers, Xixia District, Yinchuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.
Legal Representative: Fan Hailong, Chairman of the company.
Agent ad litem: Hao Zining, Lawyer of Fude Law Firm.

Appellee (Third Party at First Instance): China Petroleum Ningxia Chemical Plant. Domicile: No. 1338, West Beijing Road, Xixia District, Yinchuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.
Legal Representative: Yong Ruisheng, Director of the plant.
Agent ad litem: Hu Yonggang, Legal Counsel of the plant.
Agent ad litem: Chang Junbao, Lawyer of Desheng Law Firm.

Appellant Ningxia Yinghai Building Materials Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yinghai Group), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2009) Ning Minshang Chu Zi No. 8 rendered by the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, filed an appeal with this Court in the case of dispute over creditor's rights with Appellee Ningxia Yinghai Yinchuan Building Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yinghai Yinchuan Company) and China Petroleum Ningxia Chemical Plant (hereinafter referred to as Ningxia Chemical Plant). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Wang Dongmin, Judge Lei Jiping, and Acting Judge Liu Chongli to hear the case. Court Clerk Bai Xue served as the recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts: Yinghai Group was restructured and renamed from the sole proprietorship enterprise, Ningxia Zhongning County No. 2 Cement Plant, owned by Fan Hailong. On November 10, 1998, Ningxia Zhongning County No. 2 Cement Plant was restructured into Ningxia Yinghai Zhongning Building Materials Co., Ltd., with three shareholders: Fan Hailong, Fan Zhonghua, and Fan Zhongning (the three were father and sons), and the legal representative was Fan Hailong. On August 19, 2003, the name of Ningxia Yinghai Zhongning Building Materials Co., Ltd. was changed to Ningxia Yinghai Building Materials Group Co., Ltd., with the shareholders and legal representative unchanged. On October 16, 1998, Ningxia Zhongning County No. 2 Cement Plant and Ningxia Chemical Plant jointly invested to establish Yinghai Yinchuan Company. On November 15, 2007, Ningxia Chemical Plant filed a lawsuit with the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, requesting a judgment ordering Yinghai Yinchuan Company to distribute profits of RMB 23.585 million to Ningxia Chemical Plant and to repurchase the shares of Yinghai Yinchuan Company held by Ningxia Chemical Plant. During the trial of that case, the court commissioned an audit and appraisal institution to conduct a judicial appraisal of the profits, losses, and assets of Yinghai Yinchuan Company. Yinghai Yinchuan Company requested that the materials and cement clinker used from Yinghai Group at the time of the company's establishment be included as debts in the audit report for deduction. The audit report stated that the funds for purchased materials and the cement clinker used had not been processed in the mutual accounts, and no audit adjustment was made for the above matters. In its civil judgment (2007) Ning Minshang Chu Zi No. 33, the court did not support Yinghai Yinchuan Company's claim. Both parties were dissatisfied with the judgment and appealed to this Court. After trial, this Court issued a civil ruling (2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 162 on May 15, 2009, remanding the case for retrial. On July 1, 2009, Yinghai Group was converted into a one-person limited liability company, and the legal representative was changed to Lou Yan, the daughter-in-law of Fan Hailong.

To confirm that Yinghai Group had provided purchased materials and cement clinker to Yinghai Yinchuan Company, Yinghai Group filed this lawsuit with the court on July 15, 2009, requesting that Yinghai Yinchuan Company pay over RMB 15.43 million for materials and compensate for economic losses of RMB 5 million. Yinghai Yinchuan Company acknowledged Yinghai Group's claims and the facts and reasons thereof. On July 30, 2009, Ningxia Chemical Plant applied to participate in this lawsuit as a third party with independent claims. The court of first instance decided to allow Ningxia Chemical Plant to participate as a third party without independent claims.

The court of first instance held: In this case, Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company are two independent limited liability companies, but both are affiliated companies of the Fan family, with similar or identical business scopes, and they may have had economic dealings with each other. However, Yinghai Yinchuan Company knew or should have known that Ningxia Chemical Plant, as a shareholder, was a stakeholder of Yinghai Yinchuan Company. Over a period of ten years, regarding the company's creditor's rights and debts, it should have established a complete accounting system in accordance with the Company Law of the PRC, the Accounting Law of the PRC, and other laws, regulations, and rules. Article 164 of the Company Law provides: "A company shall establish its own financial and accounting system in accordance with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the financial department of the State Council." Article 10 of the Accounting Law provides: "The following economic business matters shall go through accounting procedures and conduct accounting calculations: ... (2) The receiving, issuing, increasing, decreasing, and use of property and materials; (3) The occurrence and settlement of creditor's rights and debts; ..." Both Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company failed to provide valid evidence to prove that they had recorded the creditor's rights and debts in accounts and conducted accounting calculations. Therefore, Yinghai Group's reliance solely on the "Temporary Material Inbound Slips," "Inbound Raw Materials or Other Materials Weighbridge Slips," and "Detailed List of Clinker Pulled by Yinchuan Company from 1999 to 2003" (hereinafter collectively referred to as the raw material slips) without other supporting evidence is insufficient to prove its factual claims, and its claims are not supported. Since there is no evidence to prove that Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company agreed on the performance period of the creditor's rights and debts, nor is there evidence to prove that Yinghai Group had ever claimed the creditor's rights and that Yinghai Yinchuan Company refused to perform the debts, the reason raised by Ningxia Chemical Plant that Yinghai Group's claims have exceeded the statute of limitations cannot be established. Pursuant to Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Procedures, the court rendered the civil judgment (2009) Ning Minshang Chu Zi No. 8, dismissing Yinghai Group's claims, and the case acceptance fee of RMB 144,309 was to be borne by Yinghai Group.

Yinghai Group, dissatisfied with the above judgment, filed an appeal with this Court, stating: (1) The court of first instance denied the existence of the creditor's rights and debts arising from the company's production and operation on the grounds that Yinghai Group's governance structure was not standardized, its accounting system was not sound, and its financial procedures were not complete. This is seriously inconsistent with the facts and is purely putting the cart before the horse. Due to the conservative thinking of the management, the accounting system was not sound, and they could not strictly manage and operate in accordance with the corporate governance structure stipulated by laws, regulations, and the company's articles of association. As a result, in economic dealings with other enterprises, especially family affiliated companies, they did not record the creditor's rights and debts that occurred according to financial procedures. However, as for the creditor's rights certificates provided by Yinghai Group, they fully comply with the basic requirements for evidence under the law. 1. The temporary material inbound slips and inbound raw materials or other materials weighbridge slips were issued by Yinghai Yinchuan Company, bearing the official seal of Yinghai Yinchuan Company. The form of the evidence is complete, and the content is true. Before Yinghai Yinchuan Company was established, Yinghai Group already had strong production capacity and had undergone several equipment upgrades and technical transformations. During the process of equipment upgrades and technical transformations, many spare parts and related materials used for cement production equipment remained. Yinghai Group delivered these materials to Yinghai Yinchuan Company for equipment addition, repair, and replacement. At the same time, the clinker production of Yinghai Yinchuan Company was unstable in quality. To ensure its normal production and operation, Yinghai Group supplied it with a large amount of cement clinker. This is an indisputable fact. 2. There is no necessary connection between the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship and whether financial accounting entries have been made. Since Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company belong to the same group company and are "family" enterprises, it is extremely normal for them to have incomplete financial procedures or even no financial processing in their transactions. If both parties wanted to fabricate false financial records, it would be very easy. 3. The conclusion of the financial audit cannot negate the objective fact that a creditor-debtor relationship existed between Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company. The factual basis of a financial audit is the financial accounts, while the basis for determining the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship is the relevant evidence. In a financial audit, even if the creditor-debtor relationship truly exists, it is a requirement of the financial system that the audit institution may find it difficult to confirm if no financial processing has been done. In the confirmation of a creditor-debtor relationship, whether the creditor holds evidence of the creditor's rights is the direct basis for confirming the existence of the creditor-debtor relationship between the parties. In this case, the existence of the creditor-debtor relationship is a legal truth. 4. Yinghai Yinchuan Company had a difficult start. Without Yinghai Group supplying the cement clinker and related items involved in this case and other forms of support, Yinghai Yinchuan Company would never have developed to its current state. (2) The court of first instance added Ningxia Chemical Plant as a third party, which was a procedural error. Article 9 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Strictly Implementing the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC in Economic Trials clearly stipulates that the court accepting the case shall not notify as a third party without independent claims any person who has no direct connection with the subject matter of the dispute between the plaintiff and the defendant and has no obligation to return or compensate, or any person who is not a party to the case and has an arbitration agreement or an agreement on jurisdiction with the plaintiff or the defendant, or any party to a case under exclusive jurisdiction. In this case, the lawsuit between Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company did not infringe upon the interests of Ningxia Chemical Plant, and Yinghai Group did not require Ningxia Chemical Plant to bear any obligation to return or compensate. Therefore, Ningxia Chemical Plant has no direct connection with this case and has no legal interest in the outcome of this case. The court of first instance's decision to add it as a third party was clearly erroneous. In summary, the first-instance judgment was erroneous in fact-finding and procedure. Appeal is requested to revoke the first-instance judgment and amend the judgment.

Yinghai Yinchuan Company acknowledged the claims and reasons of Yinghai Group.

Ningxia Chemical Plant argued in its defense: (1) The creditor's rights and debts disputed by Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company do not exist, and the first-instance judgment correctly found the facts. 1. The temporary material inbound slips totaling RMB 5,977,581.13 and the cement clinker weighbridge slips totaling RMB 9,461,331.50 submitted by Yinghai Group to the court lack supply contracts and purchase invoices. From the purchase of the bought materials and cement clinker to the handover and then to the financial recording, there is no corresponding evidence to confirm them. They cannot form a chain of evidence, and the evidence does not possess authenticity, relevance, or legality. 2. The raw material slips were not recorded in any financial accounts. For the company's creditor's rights and debts, a complete accounting system should be established in accordance with Article 164 of the Company Law of the PRC, Article 10 of the Accounting Law of the PRC, and tax laws and other regulations and rules. In this case, Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company have consistently failed to provide evidence proving that they made accounting entries and conducted accounting calculations for the creditor's rights and debts. Therefore, Yinghai Group's reliance solely on the raw material slips without other evidence to prove its factual claims clearly cannot be established. 3. Yinghai Group's claims have already been explicitly concluded by an audit. In the case of Ningxia Chemical Plant v. Yinghai Yinchuan Company, the audit report issued by the institution commissioned by the court held that the funds for purchased materials and the cement clinker provided by Yinghai Yinchuan Company had not been processed in the mutual accounts, and therefore could not be considered as payables of Yinghai Yinchuan Company and receivables of Yinghai Group. (2) The court of first instance listed Ningxia Chemical Plant as a third party, and the procedure was lawful. In this case, 40% of the subject matter disputed by Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company represents the legitimate rights and interests of Ningxia Chemical Plant and is an inseparable part of the subject matter of the case of Ningxia Chemical Plant v. Yinghai Yinchuan Company concerning profit distribution and share repurchase. The outcome of this case has a direct legal interest for Ningxia Chemical Plant. The court of first instance, in accordance with Article 56, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, listed Ningxia Chemical Plant as a third party without independent claims in this lawsuit, and the procedure was entirely lawful. In summary, the first-instance judgment correctly found the facts and was lawful in procedure. The appeal request is dismissed, and the first-instance judgment is affirmed.

During the second instance, Yinghai Group added Ningxia Chemical Plant as an appellee. None of the parties submitted new evidence.

Upon trial of the second instance, this Court confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance. This Court additionally finds: The case of Ningxia Chemical Plant v. Yinghai Yinchuan Company concerning profit distribution and share repurchase has been suspended due to this lawsuit.

This Court holds that there are two focal issues in dispute among the parties: First, whether the existing evidence in this case can prove the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship between Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company; Second, whether the court of first instance's permission for Ningxia Chemical Plant to participate in the lawsuit as a third party constitutes a procedural error.

Regarding whether the existing evidence in this case can prove the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship between Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company. Yinghai Group provided raw material slips as evidence of the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship between it and Yinghai Yinchuan Company. However, this evidence is circumstantial evidence. It can only prove that a corresponding quantity of materials and raw materials (hereinafter collectively referred to as materials) was stored by Yinghai Yinchuan Company, but it lacks evidence to prove the source, cause, and destination of the materials. It cannot prove that the materials came from Yinghai Group and were used for the production or sale of Yinghai Yinchuan Company. There is also no evidence to prove what legal relationship was established between Yinghai Yinchuan Company and Yinghai Group. Therefore, it cannot form a chain of evidence proving the formation of a creditor-debtor relationship between them, and thus cannot prove the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship between Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company. Although Yinghai Yinchuan Company admitted that it had a creditor-debtor relationship with Yinghai Group, because the existence or non-existence of this creditor-debtor relationship directly affects the interests of Ningxia Chemical Plant, another shareholder of Yinghai Yinchuan Company, and Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company are affiliated enterprises, and there is a marriage relationship between their legal representatives, and Yinghai Yinchuan Company also failed to provide other evidence to remedy the defects in Yinghai Group's evidence, this Court does not accept the statement of Yinghai Yinchuan Company admitting the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship with Yinghai Group. Furthermore, regarding the source of the materials, Yinghai Group's statements are self-contradictory. In the first instance, it stated that the materials came from Yinghai Group advancing funds to purchase on behalf of Yinghai Yinchuan Company; in the second instance, it stated that the materials came from surplus materials left over from technical transformations of Yinghai Group. In summary, the existing evidence in this case cannot prove the existence of a creditor-debtor relationship between Yinghai Group and Yinghai Yinchuan Company, and this Court does not accept Yinghai Group's claim that it had a creditor-debtor relationship with Yinghai Yinchuan Company.

Regarding whether the court of first instance's permission for Ningxia Chemical Plant to participate in the lawsuit as a third party constitutes a procedural error. Article 56, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that, with respect to the subject matter of the litigation between the parties, if a third party has no independent right to claim, but the outcome of the case has a legal interest for it, it may apply to participate in the proceedings. Since Ningxia Chemical Plant is a shareholder of Yinghai Yinchuan Company, if this case confirms that a debt owed by Yinghai Yinchuan Company to Yinghai Group exists, it will inevitably affect Ningxia Chemical Plant's profit distribution in Yinghai Yinchuan Company. Therefore, Ningxia Chemical Plant has a direct interest in the outcome of this lawsuit. Hence, the court of first instance's permission for Ningxia Chemical Plant to participate in the lawsuit as a third party complies with the legal provisions and does not constitute a procedural error. Yinghai Group's appeal argument that the first-instance procedure was erroneous is not established.

In summary, none of Yinghai Group's appeal reasons are established. The first-instance judgment correctly found the facts and applied the law correctly. This Court affirms it. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

The case acceptance fee for the first instance shall be executed in accordance with the original judgment. The case acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 144,309, to be borne by Ningxia Yinghai Building Materials Group Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Dongmin
Judge: Lei Jiping
Acting Judge: Liu Chongli
June 7, 2010
Court Clerk: Bai Xue
